counterevidence_considered.description: The input data are in long format with each mussel appearing six times (72 rows from 12 animals), so the raw table does contain repeated entries of each independent unit; if these rows had been fed directly into a row-independent test the issue class would be present. This structural risk is the only element pointing toward the issue, and it is neutralized by the within-animal aggregation performed before testing.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 72 run-level rows, 6 per mussel_id, in data/input.csv

source_refs.quoted_text:
The file `data/input.csv` is stored in long format: the same mussel appears six times,
once per clearance run.

evidence.description: The workflow collapses the six repeated clearance runs per mussel to one pre-phase mean and one post-phase mean per animal before any statistical test is run, so each independent unit (mussel_id) contributes exactly one paired row to the inferential procedure.
evidence.observed_value: per_animal_table() computes np.mean over pre runs and post runs within each mussel

evidence.description: The paired t-test is applied to the 12 per-animal pre and post means (one entry per mussel), with n = 12 and df = 11, not to the 72 run-level rows.
evidence.observed_value: stats.ttest_rel applied to arrays of length 12 built from the collapsed per-animal table; df = n - 1 = 11

evidence.description: The report's selected result states n = 12 mussels and t(11), matching an analysis at the level of the independent unit; recomputation from the raw run-level data confirms the reported per-animal means (e.g., MU-01 pre mean (3.16+3.49+3.55)/3 = 3.400) and the test statistic: the 12 within-animal changes have mean -0.9167 L/h, SD 0.2125, giving t = -0.9167/(0.2125/sqrt(12)) = -14.94 on 11 df, exactly as reported.
evidence.observed_value: reported t(11) = -14.944 reproduces from 12 independent within-animal changes

source_refs.quoted_text:
Clearance rates were averaged within animal and phase, which leaves one pre-exposure mean
and one post-exposure mean per mussel and therefore exactly one analysed row per
independent unit (`mussel_id`). The 12 within-animal changes (post minus pre) were tested
against zero with a two-sided paired t-test (`scipy.stats.ttest_rel`); the 95% interval
uses the Student t quantile on 11 degrees of freedom.

One row is: a single clearance run on one tagged mussel on one measurement day
Independent unit column: mussel_id

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show the issue is present by checking whether run-level rows leak into the test despite the report's claims. First, I traced the code path: read_runs() groups the 72 rows by mussel_id and phase, per_animal_table() reduces each group to a single mean, and stats.ttest_rel receives only the length-12 pre and post arrays, so no run-level replicate reaches the test. Second, I checked the reported degrees of freedom against what a pseudoreplicated analysis would produce: a run-level paired test on 36 pre/post pairs (or 72 rows) would give df around 35 or 70, but the report states t(11), consistent only with 12 analysed units. Third, I recomputed the statistic from the raw CSV: the 12 within-animal changes (-0.900, -0.700, -1.200, -0.800, -1.000, -0.600, -1.100, -0.900, -1.300, -0.800, -1.000, -0.700) have mean -0.9167 and SD 0.2125, yielding t = -14.94 on 11 df, matching the reported value exactly; a run-level analysis would not reproduce this SD or t. All three checks failed to demonstrate the issue, so the conclusion as stated is supported by an analysis performed at the correct independent-unit level.
